text:
Minnesota won 4-1, but the numbers say Boston played the better game. The Bruins held the edge at even strength in expected goals (1.83 to 1.41), and in simulated replays of every shot, BOS wins 56 percent of the time. The gap in the total (MIN 3.53, BOS 2.70) comes from the power play, where the Wild went 2 for 3 and the Bruins went 0 for 3.

Tanner Jeannot gave Boston the lead 1:53 into the game, but the Wild answered in the second period on the man advantage. Kirill Kaprizov tied it with a snap shot at 6:11, then Quinn Hughes put Minnesota ahead at 12:28 with a wrist shot that carried only a 6 percent chance of scoring. That was the swing of the game: a low-probability shot on a power play turned a Boston-leaning game into a Minnesota lead. Jared Spurgeon added a third at 3:24 of the third period on a 1 percent chance, and Kaprizov closed it at 18:59 with a backhand.

The other piece was in goal. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 26 of 27 shots, about 1.7 goals better than expected, and took first star. Michael DiPietro faced 29 shots for Boston and gave up three goals against an expected 2.39. Boston generated 2.70 expected goals and had only the Jeannot goal to show for it. Kaprizov finished with two goals and the best underlying numbers of any skater, 1.97 expected goals for against 0.35 against while he was on the ice.
